=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:78-83 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts any HTTPS URL on github.com without verifying that the repository path matches the trusted repository identity.
  WHY: An editor can change origin to an attacker-controlled repository, after which restore embeds GH_TOKEN in that URL.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:76-84 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore checks only the first configured origin URL and can inject credentials even when additional origin URLs are present.
  WHY: An attacker-controlled secondary URL evades validation, and the tests asserting rejection of multiple origin URLs fail.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:85-93 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore writes extraheaders back to their original keys instead of scoping authorization to the verified origin repository.
  WHY: A generic extraheader applies to other GitHub requests and can expose the authorization token beyond the trusted repository.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:87 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The extraheader key validation checks only its format and does not ensure its path matches the verified origin repository.
  WHY: An extraheader key scoped to an attacker-controlled repository passes validation and receives the restored token.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:19-54 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide and restore do not validate push URLs or `pushInsteadOf` rewrites.
  WHY: Credentials can remain exposed in a push URL, or pushes can be redirected to an unauthorized destination; severity disagreement: reviewers rated this BLOCKER and MAJOR, and the highest rating is used.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:19-102 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Credential-helper failure paths return success, including failures to hide or restore credentials and restore without GH_TOKEN.
  WHY: Callers continue as though credential isolation succeeded, potentially launching the editor with credentials still available; severity disagreement: reviewers rated this BLOCKER and MAJOR, and the highest rating is used.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:56 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore without a marker does not emit the expected `reason=marker_missing` diagnostic.
  WHY: The missing-marker condition is indistinguishable in logs from a successful no-op; severity disagreement: reviewers rated this BLOCKER and MAJOR, and the highest rating is used.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:19-24 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide returns success when an unrestored marker already exists instead of failing.
  WHY: A subsequent restore may use stale marker data to restore credentials that were not hidden in the current session; severity disagreement: reviewers rated this BLOCKER and MAJOR, and the highest rating is used.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:19-54 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide does not validate trusted repository identity before operating on credentials.
  WHY: Credential hiding can proceed without confirming that the checkout belongs to the expected repository.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:61-97 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore injects tokens into checkouts as it processes them rather than validating all checkouts first.
  WHY: A token can be injected into an earlier checkout before a later editor-changed checkout is rejected.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:484-491 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: With `--repo` and multiple bare refspecs, push parsing drops the first positional refspec.
  WHY: The guard can fail to check the first pushed branch for merged-PR state and allow a push it should block.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:483-491 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: With `--repo` and multiple bare refspecs, the template push guard drops the first positional refspec.
  WHY: The guard can fail to check the first pushed branch for merged-PR state and allow a push it should block.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:484-487 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: A single bare refspec matching a configured remote name can be treated as a remote rather than as the branch being pushed.
  WHY: The guard checks HEAD instead of the intended branch, potentially allowing a merged-branch push or blocking an unrelated push; severity disagreement: reviewers rated this MAJOR and NIT, and the highest rating is used.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:484-487 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: A single bare refspec matching a configured remote name can be treated as a remote rather than as the branch being pushed.
  WHY: The template guard checks HEAD instead of the intended branch, potentially allowing a merged-branch push or blocking an unrelated push; severity disagreement: reviewers rated this MAJOR and NIT, and the highest rating is used.
- tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:95-105 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The multiple-origin-URLs contract test fails because restore reads only the first origin URL and returns success after injecting the token.
  WHY: CI runs the isolation test suite, so this failing assertion blocks the PR.
- tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:108-117 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The extraheader-scoping contract test fails because restore writes the header to its original generic key rather than the scoped origin key.
  WHY: CI runs the isolation test suite, so this failing assertion blocks the PR.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:38-41 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The review autofix workspace filter on main may drop `scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh` because it lacks the credential-path exemption.
  WHY: Automated review-fix commits may be unable to transfer updates to the credential helper back to the checkout.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:484-491 and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:484-491 | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The `--repo` handling adds a `git remote` subprocess call on the push-guard hot path in a narrow case.
  WHY: No runtime failure was identified; the reviewer states the call has a timeout, uses `_git_environment`, and is validated by a test.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: AD-1 — "Remove credentials only: drop GH_TOKEN, GH_PAT, Telegram and other non-model secrets from the editor's environment at both implement editor launches (main loop and syntax repair). The editor keeps the network access the model needs. Pin this with a contract test."
  expected_change_site: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh and tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The helper omits GITHUB_REPOSITORY validation, pushURL and pushInsteadOf checks, multiple-origin-URL detection, extraheader scoping, `reason=marker_missing`, non-zero exits on failures, and pre-validation of all checkouts before injecting tokens; the contract tests exercise these missing behaviors and fail against the current helper.
- requirement: AD-4 — "When heal evidence was put in the prompt, fail closed if the issue or plan has no files_touched allowlist, and turn off the ALLOW_OUT_OF_SCOPE_FILES override for that run."
  expected_change_site: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The scope-lock wiring in implement.yml and implement_commit_changes.sh is present and correct, but the credential helper's unconditional `exit 0` means credential-isolation failures do not fail the editor step.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:76-84 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts any origin URL that starts with `https://github.com/` without verifying it matches the workflow repository, and the test expecting rejection of multiple origin URLs fails.
  WHY: An editor can add a secondary origin URL pointing to an attacker repo alongside the legitimate origin and receive GH_TOKEN injection.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:85-93 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore writes extraheaders back to their original keys rather than deriving a scoped key from the verified origin.
  WHY: A generic extraheader key sends the authorization header on any GitHub request, not only those to the verified origin.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:102 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The script unconditionally exits 0 regardless of credential operation failures.
  WHY: Workflow steps continue as though credentials were restored successfully when they were not.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:87 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The extraheader key regex validates only format and does not verify the path component matches the workflow repository's origin.
  WHY: An extraheader stored under an attacker-controlled path passes the regex and receives the token.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:56 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore without a marker exits silently instead of emitting the `reason=marker_missing` diagnostic.
  WHY: A missing-marker restore is indistinguishable from a successful no-op restore in logs.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:484-491 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: With `--repo` and multiple positionals, the parser drops the first branch and does not check it for a merged PR.
  WHY: A push of two branches through `--repo` only checks the second branch, allowing an undetected push onto merged history through the first branch.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:57-59 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore exits 0 when GH_TOKEN is missing.
  WHY: The workflow cannot distinguish successful restore from failure because the secret was unavailable.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:19-54 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hide does not validate `pushurl`, `url.*.pushInsteadOf`, or `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` identity before stripping credentials.
  WHY: An alternate push destination can receive credentials, or credential hiding can proceed without trusted repository identity.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:484-487 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A bare branch name matching a configured remote can cause refspecs to be empty, so the guard checks HEAD instead of the intended branch.
  WHY: The guard may allow a push of a branch on merged history or block a push based on an unrelated
